notes: I judged all 49 claims against worktree W at cb398676. 21 conform. 28 do not, and every one of those is drift: a later log entry records the move. Most are renames: faces->passthrough (D-144, D-251); Merged/merge->Combined/combine (D-204, which also says the log keeps its day's vocabulary); the *_connections names->local_wires/input_wires/output_wires (D-279, D-303, D-314); input_types/output_types/output_state->u_types/y_types/y_state (D-267); sweep_hx/sweep_hxu->sweep_1/sweep_2 (D-196); RootSlotTypeConflict->RootInputTypeConflict (D-206); Dataflow->Outputs (D-261); Period/Hz retired (D-469); stop_on->StopFlag (D-316). The rest change what the code does: D-414 dropped the deep-`at` locality check; D-445 rewrote how the due set is computed; D-205 changed boundary zero, where updates stay gated; D-437 made return shapes follow bare contracts, which affects Constant, the NamedTuple check and DeadStage. I found no deviation, defect or gap. L6d-185 is the closest call: I passed it because the handler-return key check mirrors the FieldError law, though it shares no code with it. The probe script is /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/L6d_v/probe.jl, run once. I edited no tracked file and committed nothing.
